title: The Fate of an Objection
corpus_scope: ICLR 2018–2026 · 551,595 objections raised by official reviewers
question: When a reviewer raises an objection, is it ever revisited after the authors respond — and if so, does the judgment soften or harden?

figures.title: Raised → revisited → softened / hardened, per object
figures.deck: 92% of objections are never mentioned again. Of the 8% that are, most stand unchanged — and when the judgment does move, it hardens 2.5× more often than it softens.

claims.derivation: sum of .raised over all 12 objects in LIFECYCLE.objects = 551,595

claims.statement: 92.1% of objections occupy the near-empty span — the same reviewer never mentions them again — with 6.5% revisited but unmoved, 1.0% hardened and 0.4% softened.
claims.derivation: share of the 551,595 objections whose own reviewer never mentions the object again after the author response

claims.statement: Hardening outruns softening for every object — from 1.5× (novelty) to 3.2× (clarity), 2.5× overall.
claims.derivation: per-object harden_given_revisit ÷ soften_given_revisit ratio, ranked across the 12 objects; overall ratio computed from LIFECYCLE totals

claims.statement: Related-work objections are the most revisited (11.7% — a citation fix is checkable), and novelty objections harden the least (8.0% of revisits).
claims.derivation: LIFECYCLE.objects.related_work.revisit_rate (max across 12 objects) and LIFECYCLE.objects.novelty harden-given-revisit share (min across 12)

figures.title: The interrogative: does an objection asked fare differently from one asserted?
figures.deck: Asked or asserted, an objection meets the same fate — revisited at 5.1% vs 5.2%, a null result reported as one. The only thing that moves the needle is raising it in both fields (7.4%): intensity, not grammar.

claims.statement: Objections phrased as questions are revisited at 5.1% against 5.2% for those asserted as statements — a null result, reported as one.
claims.derivation: share of 2026 objections revisited after the response, split by whether the objection was phrased as a question ([questions] field, 13,568) or asserted ([weaknesses] field, 85,343)

claims.statement: An objection raised in both fields is revisited at 7.4% and hardens at 1.1% — what moves the needle is intensity, not grammar.
claims.derivation: ov.both[key] for key='revisit' and key='harden', among the 5,151 objections raised in both the weaknesses and questions fields

caveats.text: A revisited objection is counted only when the same reviewer's own text names the object again after the response; a score quietly changed without a word of text is invisible to this measure, and every recorded fate is a model's reading of prose.
